questions.stem: When is data modelling with graph theory particularly useful?
options: When relationships between data points are as important as the data itself
When the data consists of a single flat table
When there are no relationships between records
When data only needs to be archived
When the data is purely numeric
questions.explanation: Graph modelling is particularly useful when the relationships between data points are as important as the data itself, such as in social networks or knowledge graphs.

questions.stem: In data modelling with graphs, how are data entities and their connections represented?
options: Entities as columns and connections as rows
Entities as nodes and connections as edges
Entities as edges and connections as nodes
Entities as files and connections as folders
Entities as keys and connections as indexes
questions.explanation: Each data entity is represented as a node and each connection between entities is modelled as an edge, such as a 'Friend' relationship between users.

questions.stem: Which graph-based data model uses triples of subject, predicate and object, and is common in the semantic web and knowledge graphs?
questions.explanation: The RDF Graph Model uses triples such as Alice, Knows, Bob and is commonly used in the semantic web and knowledge graphs.

questions.stem: What is distinctive about a hypergraph?
options: It stores data only as triples
Its edges can connect more than two nodes
It is used only by Neo4j
questions.explanation: In a hypergraph, edges can connect more than two nodes, for example a single edge connecting all the members of a group.

questions.stem: In the Property Graph Model used by graph databases such as Neo4j, what do nodes and edges carry?
options: Properties as key-value pairs, such as Name: Alice, Age: 25 on a node and Since: 2020 on an edge
questions.explanation: In the Property Graph Model both nodes and edges have properties expressed as key-value pairs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the steps for modelling data with graph theory?
options: Normalise all data into third normal form
questions.explanation: The steps are to identify entities and relationships, define node and edge types, determine attributes and properties, optimise for queries and choose a graph database; normalising to 3NF is a relational technique.

questions.stem: In the e-commerce graph model example, which of the following is an edge rather than a node?
questions.explanation: Customers, Products and Categories are nodes; 'Buys', 'Reviews' and 'Belongs To' are the edges connecting them.

questions.stem: What does 'Optimise for Queries' recommend when modelling a graph for an e-commerce platform?
options: Removing all edges to simplify the graph
Storing every product in a single node
Adding direct edges for frequent queries, such as 'Customers who bought X also bought Y'
Converting the graph into a spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Designing the graph for efficient common operations can mean adding direct edges for frequent queries such as product recommendations.

questions.stem: Which application of graph data modelling involves analysing transaction networks to detect unusual patterns or cycles?
questions.explanation: Fraud detection analyses transaction networks to identify fraudulent activity, such as unusual patterns or cycles in financial transactions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a challenge of graph-based data modelling?
options: The learning curve of graph query languages such as Cypher, Gremlin and SPARQL
questions.explanation: The challenges named are complexity, scalability and the learning curve of graph query languages such as Cypher, Gremlin and SPARQL.
